subtype: Approach: keeping a running record of achievements [Action]
passage:
Looking back, the thing that changed my review was a plain file. The year before, I could barely remember what I'd done between January and June. So on the last day of every month I started a note: what I delivered, numbers if I had them, and any kind words. March: the invoice report that saved the finance team forty hours. April: a thank-you line from Naveen, my manager, about the client demo. When review season came and Naveen asked, "What have you achieved this year?", I didn't have to search my memory. I scrolled through the note and read out six items. It took ten minutes and felt like a conversation about facts, not about how well I recalled the year. I still write it every month.

Maria

qa.q: How many items did Maria read out in the review?
How did Maria feel in the review after keeping the note?
qa.a: Maria felt calm and prepared, since there was no need to search memory.

qa.q: What else could Maria add to the note, and why?
qa.a: Maria could add a line on what was learned each month, because it shows growth as well as results.

qa.q: How might Naveen have found the review conversation?
qa.a: Naveen probably found it easier and clearer, since specific facts gave the discussion something solid to talk about.

grounding: Illustrates keeping a monthly note of delivered work, numbers and feedback so review conversations are concrete rather than memory based.

Manager's note, annual review file — Kiran, operations analyst

I want to record how Kiran prepared for this year's review, because it made my job easier.
From April, Kiran kept a one-page note at the end of each month: what was delivered, any numbers, and any feedback received. In June it lists the vendor report she automated, which saved the finance team about forty hours a month, with a thank-you email from Mridul in accounts attached. In September it shows the dashboard she rebuilt after two complaints.
In our review meeting, instead of both of us trying to remember the year, she opened the file and walked me through twelve pages. We spent our time on what next, not what happened.
What I did next: I forwarded the June and September pages to the promotion panel, and I've suggested the team try the same monthly habit.

qa.q: How many hours a month did Kiran's automated report save the finance team?
How might Kiran have felt opening the file in the review meeting?
qa.a: Kiran likely felt confident and calm, because the monthly notes meant the achievements were already written down instead of relying on memory.

qa.q: What else could Kiran add to the monthly notes to make them even stronger?
qa.a: Kiran could add a line on what each piece of work taught her or what she'd do differently, so the panel sees growth as well as results.

qa.q: How does Kiran's record affect the manager writing the note?
qa.a: The manager can spend the review on the future and forward specific pages to the promotion panel, rather than trying to recall a whole year.

grounding: It shows someone keeping a monthly record of delivered work, numbers and feedback, which makes the review conversation concrete rather than memory based.

passage:
31 October

Month-end ritual done. Sat on the balcony with ginger tea and wrote this month's page for my record:
- Finished the supplier audit two days early.
- Cut the returns backlog from 300 cases to 80.
- Harsha said in the team meeting that my process guide "should be the standard". Writing it down before I forget she said it.

Honestly, I started this in January because last year's review was a disaster. Harsha asked what I'd achieved, and my mind went blank. I mumbled something about "being busy". I was so embarrassed.
This year I have ten pages. It feels a bit dry, writing facts like a clerk, but when the review comes I'll be pointing at numbers, not scrambling.
Next month: add the training session I'm running for new joiners.
— Jyoti

qa.q: What did Jyoti cut the returns backlog to?
How did Jyoti feel in last year's review, and why?
qa.a: Jyoti felt embarrassed, because when Harsha asked about achievements, Jyoti's mind went blank and all that came out was "being busy".

qa.q: What would you add to Jyoti's approach before the next review?
qa.a: Jyoti could ask Harsha which achievements matter most for the next level, so the monthly record collects the right evidence, not only everything.

qa.q: How might Harsha see the record at review time?
qa.a: Harsha gets concrete numbers and dates to discuss, so the review is easier to judge fairly and less dependent on what Harsha happens to remember.

grounding: It shows someone writing a monthly note of delivered work, numbers and feedback so review conversations become concrete rather than memory based.
